page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8a.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 8 physical AMD EPYC 9T24 cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 7 Gbps.

The underlying AMD EPYC architecture supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 vector extensions (AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16) and hardware-accelerated cryptography (AES, VAES, and SHA_NI). In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong single-core performance, scoring in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core CPU tests and Geekbench single-core metrics. Multi-core performance, including Passmark CPU and Geekbench multi-core scores, falls within the average range.

Memory performance presents a notable tradeoff. While cached small-block read-only memory bandwidth is average at 1216.93 GB/sec, large-block uncached read-only memory bandwidth is weak, measuring 39.07 GB/sec and placing in the bottom 25%. This makes the instance less suitable for memory-bound workloads with large, uncached datasets. However, with solid text processing, static web serving, and database operation benchmarks, this instance is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, including web serving, application hosting, software compilation, and moderate database operations.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8a.4xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor running at 2.7 GHz. Utilizing the KVM hypervisor, this x86_64 server provides a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests. However, a key tradeoff is its uncached large-block read memory bandwidth, which falls into the bottom 25% at 39.07 GB/sec. Conversely, cached memory reads and multi-core operations perform at average levels. With a baseline network bandwidth of 7 Gbps and support for AVX-512 and cryptographic instructions, this instance is suited for general-purpose workloads such as web serving, application hosting, software compilation, and standard database operations.
